Tabelog could not be checked: as of 2026-09-02 it still returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge body to both curl and WebFetch, so its page for this shop is UNVERIFIED rather than empty and its URL is deliberately absent from sources. ⚠ TWO USEFUL THINGS THE SHOP STATES OUTRIGHT. First, 半ライス無料！！おかわりもっ！！ — HALF A BOWL OF RICE IS FREE, and refillable. Plain rice is the one thing in a ramen shop that carries no wheat, so a coeliac accompanying other people here has something to eat that costs nothing, which is worth knowing even though it is not a meal. Second, the shop descends from なりたけ (なりたけから独立) and its miso tare is 秘伝 inherited from there. ⚠ THAT MISO IS THE HIDDEN QUESTION ON THIS MENU. Six of the eleven items are miso bowls, and Japanese miso is frequently 麦味噌 — fermented on BARLEY. 麦 is not on Japan’s statutory allergen list, so a barley miso is never declared as an allergen anywhere in this country, and a 秘伝 recipe is by definition one the shop will not break down. ⚠ AND ONE NOODLE DESCRIPTION IS WORTH READING TWICE: the あっさり中華そば uses 全粒粉入の細麺 — noodles made with WHOLEMEAL flour. 全粒粉 reads as the health-conscious choice and is sometimes mistaken for a grain swap; it is wheat, milled whole. This is the shop’s lighter bowl and it is no better for a coeliac than the heavy ones. Nothing on this menu suits a vegan: the style is pork back fat, the chashu is house-made, and even the noodles are wheat.

tokyo_toriyaki_hajime.price_note: No dish and no price, and this is an honest empty reached the hard way rather than by giving up early. The shop has its own site and its own menu page, and that page links two PDFs — menu.pdf (880KB) and drink.pdf (735KB). Both were downloaded and both were extracted. ⚠ THEY HAVE A TEXT LAYER AND IT IS STILL UNUSABLE, which is a different failure from a scan and worth recording precisely: the Japanese characters do not survive extraction at all. What comes out of an 880KB food menu is 483 non-whitespace characters, consisting of the postcode 101-0061, the street number 2-18-2, the phone and fax number 03-3288-0031, the email, the URL, and the opening hours 11:30–14:00 / 17:00–23:00 — every ASCII character on the page and not one dish. The rest of the file renders as dotted leader lines, the row of dots that runs between a dish name and its price on a printed menu, which is the shape of the menu with all of its content removed. The prices are laid out as glyphs too and did not come through either. So the menu is published, it is public, it is not a photograph, and it still cannot be read. Nothing has been taken from the shape of it. Tabelog could not be checked: as of 2026-09-02 it still returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge body to both curl and WebFetch, so its page for this shop is UNVERIFIED rather than empty and its URL is deliberately absent from sources. ⚠ WHAT THE HTML PAGE ITSELF STATES: dinner only, 月〜土 17:00–23:00, closed Sundays and public holidays, 11 counter seats and 12 at tables — a small counter shop. The PDF’s hours line suggests a lunch service too, and the site has a separate lunch.html, so the two disagree; the HTML menu page is the more recently maintained of the two and is what is recorded here. ⚠ ORIENTATION ONLY, since nothing about this kitchen is sourced: とり焼 is chicken grilling, and the one question that decides a yakitori order for a coeliac is タレ or 塩 — a tare glaze is soy sauce, mirin and sugar and is painted on during cooking, while 塩 is salt. Salt-grilled skewers are the standard route, but whether this shop offers each skewer both ways is exactly what an unreadable menu cannot say. Re-check if the shop ever republishes the menu as HTML.

tokyo_brisk_stand_suidobashi.price_note: Full menu with prices, read from the shop’s own official site and the complete menu listing it links to — burgers, sets, toppings, hamburg plates, sides, desserts and the whole drinks list. The listing states there is no course menu, no lunch menu and no takeaway menu. Tabelog was not consulted: as of 2026-09-03 it returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge, so its page is unverified rather than empty and its URL is absent from sources. Many items are marked 水道橋限定, exclusive to this branch. ⚠ A BURGER BAR IS A CLOSED DOOR FOR A COELIAC AND THIS ONE OFFERS NO GLUTEN-FREE BUN, so that is stated plainly rather than worked around. What makes the record worth reading is the SECOND wheat source, which this shop prints in its own item names and which almost nobody reads as an ingredient: eleven of the burgers are listed as 生わさび醤油付き — served with fresh wasabi and SOY SAUCE. Someone who has already accepted they cannot eat the bun, or who orders a patty without one, is still being handed a dip brewed with wheat. The 生 in 生わさび refers to the wasabi being fresh rather than tubed; it says nothing about the soy. ⚠ AND THE FRYER IS SHARED AND DEMONSTRABLY SO. This kitchen fries battered ONION RINGS and battered FISH AND CHIPS alongside its 生ポテトチップス and ポテトフライ, all on the same branch-exclusive side menu — so the chips are a shared-oil problem, not a maybe. ⚠ FOR A VEGAN THERE IS NOTHING ON THE FOOD MENU AT ALL: every burger is beef or chicken, the hamburg plates are beef, the salads are dressed and one is a Cobb, and the only meat-free items are the pickles and the potato sides. The drinks list has one specific trap worth naming — カルピス, in the sour, the water and the soda, is a FERMENTED MILK concentrate. It reads as a soft drink and it is dairy.

tokyo_raoma_hinabebou.price_note: Full hotpot and à la carte menus with prices, tax included, read from the shop’s own site. The course and drinks pages exist and are not itemised here. A TABLE CHARGE of ¥423 per person applies, and there is a two-hour limit when busy. Tabelog was not consulted: as of 2026-09-03 it returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge, so its page is unverified rather than empty and its URL is absent from sources. 渋谷; the shop states 国産野菜 常時40種類以上, 肉10種類以上, ラム肉 部位別に4種類, つけダレ約30種類, and that heat is chosen at the table from 0 to 5. ⚠ THIS IS PROBABLY THE STRONGEST VENUE IN THE TOKYO SET FOR A VEGAN, AND FOR AN UNUSUAL STRUCTURAL REASON: at a hotpot restaurant the customer assembles the meal from individually priced RAW INGREDIENTS. Nine leafy vegetables, ten roots, sixteen mushrooms, tofu in five forms, yuba, and three kinds of glass noodle are each sold on their own. Nobody has to ask the kitchen to leave anything out, because nothing is combined until it reaches the table. A plant-eater can build a genuinely large meal here from the menu as printed, which is true of almost nothing else in this dataset. ⚠ AND THE WHOLE THING TURNS ON ONE UNANSWERED QUESTION: THE BROTH. The shop advertises 無添加・無着色 and a 薬膳 medicinal base, but 無添加 is a claim about additives — it is not an allergen claim and not a vegan one, exactly like the 化学調味料不使用 claim at 叶屋 elsewhere in this dataset. Nothing published says whether the stock is built on chicken or pork bones, and a Sichuan 麻辣 base is conventionally made with beef tallow. Since every ingredient below is cooked in that pot, one question at the counter decides the entire menu — ask it before ordering anything. The shop offers a single-person pot at ¥2,200, which is the practical way to get a broth of your own. ⚠ THE GLASS NOODLES ARE A REAL FIND. Where a hotpot 〆 is normally 中華麺 — wheat — this shop also sells 緑豆春雨 (MUNG BEAN), さつまいも春雨 and さつまいも板春雨 (SWEET POTATO), all naturally wheat-free, plus 豆腐干絲, shredded dried tofu, which works as a noodle too. So the finisher, usually the moment a coeliac has to stop eating, is available here in three wheat-free forms. ⚠ ON THE ~30 DIPPING SAUCES, THE SPLIT IS SHARP AND WORTH LEARNING. Anything ending in 醬 — 麻辣醬, 生姜醬, 香辣醬, 辣椒醬, 沙茶醬, にら醬, 芝麻醬 — is a fermented paste, and Chinese fermented pastes are normally made with WHEAT FLOUR; the same goes for the house ごまだれ, which is sesame loosened with soy. But the shop also sells single condiments: ごま油 ¥121, 一味唐辛子 ¥121, 粉山椒 ¥330, おろしニンニク ¥220, 長葱みじん ¥220, 香菜 ¥385 and four vinegars. Sesame oil, chilli, sanshō, garlic, spring onion and coriander make a complete Sichuan dip with no wheat and nothing animal in it. ⚠ ONE SAUCE IS A SPECIFIC VEGAN TRAP: 沙茶醬 (sacha) is built on DRIED SHRIMP and dried fish despite reading as a bean paste. And 腐乳, which sounds like an animal product, is fermented BEAN CURD and is plant.

items.note: ⚠ THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT ITEM ON THIS MENU, BECAUSE EVERYTHING ELSE IS COOKED IN IT. tokyo_shibuya_khao_man_gai.price_note: NO PRICES, ONE DISH — and yet this is one of the more useful records in the set, because of what the shop writes about its own ingredients. 渋谷カオマンガイ is a カオマンガイ専門店, a single-dish shop, and its site carries no priced menu: the only menu links it offers go to Demae-can delivery pages, which were attempted and did not respond at all (connection failure, no HTTP status), so nothing has been taken from them. Tabelog was not consulted: as of 2026-09-03 it returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge, so its page is unverified rather than empty and its URL is absent from sources. The shop runs delivery-only branches elsewhere and a related gapao brand, ガパオガイ, neither of which is this record. ⚠ WHY THIS MATTERS OUT OF PROPORTION TO ITS ONE ITEM: KHAO MAN GAI IS THE DISH MOST OFTEN RECOMMENDED TO COELIACS IN THAI FOOD. Poached chicken on rice with a bowl of clear broth has no noodle, no batter, no fryer and no obvious sauce — it is the standard answer to "what can I eat at a Thai place", and it is repeated in guidebooks and forums constantly. This shop describes exactly how it makes each of the three components, and two of the three descriptions close the door. ⚠ FIRST, THE RICE IS NOT NEUTRAL. The shop writes: 鶏肉をゆでたときにできたチキンスープで炊きあげることで、うまみたっぷりのごはんになります — the jasmine rice is COOKED IN THE CHICKEN STOCK. That is the entire point of the dish and it is also the reason a vegan cannot order "just the rice". A plate of rice and vegetables at this shop is still made of chicken. ⚠ SECOND, THE SAUCE IS SOY, AND THE SHOP SAYS SO. Its description of the 特製ソース is 「タイの味噌、醤油、黒酢醤油を混ぜ合わせ発酵させる事で独特の深みを追求」 — Thai miso, SOY SAUCE and black-vinegar SOY SAUCE, blended and fermented together, with garlic, ginger and chilli. Three fermented soy products in one sauce, and Japanese soy sauce is brewed with WHEAT. The sauce is not a condiment on the side here; it is what the shop presents as the thing it researched and got right. ⚠ THIRD, THE ONE COMPONENT THAT DOES SURVIVE: the chicken itself is 国産ハーブ鶏 simmered gently in water — poached meat and nothing else — and the soup served alongside is described as チキンスープをベースにした塩味のオリジナルスープ, seasoned with SALT rather than soy. So a coeliac who asks for the chicken and the broth without the sauce, and accepts that the rice is cooked in stock rather than water, has a real meal here. That is a conversation worth having at the counter, and it is a different conversation from the one this dish’s reputation would suggest.

items.section: カオマンガイ Khao man gai
items.note: ⚠ THE SAUCE IS THE WHEAT, AND THE SHOP NAMES ITS INGREDIENTS ITSELF: タイの味噌、醤油、黒酢醤油 — Thai miso, soy sauce and black-vinegar soy sauce, fermented together — so the signature sauce is three soy products deep, and Japanese soy sauce is brewed with wheat. ⚠ THE RICE IS THE ANIMAL PART: the shop states the jasmine rice is 鶏肉をゆでたときにできたチキンスープで炊きあげる, cooked in the chicken stock, so there is no version of this plate that is plant-based even without the meat. What is clean is the chicken — 国産ハーブ鶏 poached in water — and the accompanying soup, which the shop describes as 塩味, salt-seasoned, rather than soy. Ask for it without the sauce. No price is published anywhere on the shop’s site, so the field is empty rather than guessed.

tokyo_tokyo_mercato_tokyo_dome.price_note: Full dinner, lunch and party-plan menus with prices, read from the shop’s own official site — the operator publishes each menu section as a separate tab and all three were fetched. The site states repeatedly that 表示価格はすべて税込み価格です, all prices include tax. The drinks tab was not read and drinks are therefore not recorded. 文京区後楽1-3-61, Tokyo Dome City Meets Port 3F, no closing day, 11:00–22:00. Tabelog could not be checked: as of 2026-09-03 it still returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge body to both curl and WebFetch, so its page for this shop is UNVERIFIED rather than empty and its URL is deliberately absent from sources. ⚠ A NAPOLETANA PIZZERIA WITH A WOOD-FIRED OVEN IS A CLOSED DOOR FOR A COELIAC and this one offers no gluten-free base or pasta, so that is said plainly. What makes the record worth reading is one item that settles everything else: 漁師風ゼッポリーネ, which the shop describes as もっちりとしたピザ生地にあおさと海苔を練り込み、カリッと香ばしく揚げた — PIZZA DOUGH kneaded with seaweed and DEEP-FRIED. That means the fryer is a wheat fryer, and it takes the chips, the seafood fritto and the arancini with it. ⚠ THE OTHER THING TO KNOW IS THAT THE ANTIPASTI ARE WHERE THIS RESTAURANT IS ACTUALLY EDIBLE. Cured ham, buffalo mozzarella, a three-cheese board, seasonal pickles, marinated olives, octopus and tomato, carpaccio, caprese — none of these has flour in it, and they are the cheapest things on the menu. A coeliac can build a real meal here from the cold section, skip the two headline categories entirely, and finish with the panna cotta, which is the one dessert with no biscuit anywhere in it. ⚠ FOR A VEGAN THE MENU IS NEARLY CLOSED BUT NOT QUITE, AND THE EXCEPTION IS WORTH NAMING: ピッツァ・マリナーラ. The shop describes it as トマトソース、にんにく、オレガノ、オリーブオイルのみ — tomato, garlic, oregano and olive oil ONLY. A marinara is the one classical Neapolitan pizza with NO CHEESE, so its topping is entirely plant while its base is entirely wheat: the two diets fail on opposite halves of the same dish. Beyond that a vegan has the olives at ¥450, the seasonal pickles at ¥500, and the arrabbiata if the kitchen leaves the parmesan off. ⚠ AND TWO DISHES CARRY WHEAT THAT ARRIVES BESIDE THEM RATHER THAN IN THEM: the chicken liver pâté is listed as 鶏レバーのパテ〜メルバトースト添え〜, served WITH melba toast, and the shop sells that toast separately at ¥200 and a baguette at ¥220. Asking for the pâté without its toast is the difference.

tokyo_charu_mogossoyo_tokyo_do.price_note: No dish and no price. The shop has an official page on its operator’s site and a brand page above it; both were fetched and read in full, and neither publishes a single menu item. The shop page has navigation labelled コース, 料理, ドリンク and ランチ but the content behind those labels is not in the served HTML, and /menu/, /food/ and /course/ under the shop path all return HTTP 404. There is no PDF and no separate menu host. Tabelog could not be checked: as of 2026-09-03 it still returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge body to both curl and WebFetch, so its page for this shop is UNVERIFIED rather than empty and its URL is deliberately absent from sources. ⚠ WHAT THE PAGE DOES ESTABLISH, and some of it is operationally useful even with no dishes: this is a NEW OPENING — a Korean 酒場 that opened 13 November in the FOOD STADIUM TOKYO food hall on the second floor of the 黄色いビル at Tokyo Dome City. It is inside a FOOD COURT of roughly 480 shared seats, takes no reservations, has no cover or service charge, opens 11:00–23:00 with no closing day, and the operator states a budget from ¥980. Wheelchair access and accessible toilets are available and foreign-language service is offered. The name チャルモゴッソヨ (잘 먹었어요) means "I ate well". ⚠ NOTHING ABOUT WHAT IT SERVES IS RECORDED, deliberately. The page describes it as 本格的な韓国料理 with SNS-friendly drinks including チャミスル and 推しカラードリンク, and that is a marketing description, not a menu — inferring gochujang, ramyeon or jeon from the words "Korean food" is precisely the reasoning this dataset forbids. ⚠ ONE STRUCTURAL POINT WORTH CARRYING, since it follows from the venue rather than the menu: a FOOD COURT stall shares its seating and often its fryers and washing with neighbouring counters, and its staff are the least able to answer an ingredient question at a rush. Re-check when the operator publishes a menu or when Tabelog access returns.

tokyo_rokumei_coffee_shibuya_s.price_note: Full café menu with prices, tax included, read from the roaster’s own shop page for this branch — the complete DRINK and FOOD lists as the counter serves them. The same site sells beans and gifts by mail order; those are retail products rather than café items and are not recorded here. 渋谷区渋谷2-24-12 Shibuya Scramble Square 2F, 8:00–21:00 (9:00–21:00 weekends and holidays), with the note that before 10:00 it is TAKEAWAY AND RETAIL ONLY. A six-seat counter with a barista on duty; the branch opened 5 March 2026 as the roaster’s second Kanto shop. Tabelog was not consulted: as of 2026-09-03 it returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge, so its page is unverified rather than empty and its URL is absent from sources. ⚠ THE SIMPLEST GOOD NEWS IN THIS DATASET: A SPECIALTY COFFEE COUNTER IS ONE OF THE VERY FEW PLACES WHERE A COELIAC AND A VEGAN CAN BOTH ORDER WITHOUT A CONVERSATION. Black coffee is roasted bean and water. Eleven of the drinks here — the six named blends, the single origins, the espresso, the americano and both cold brews — clear both diets outright, and the cheapest is ¥500. ⚠ THE FOOD LIST IS THE OPPOSITE, AND IT IS SHORT ENOUGH TO STATE COMPLETELY: four items, all four of them WHEAT. Two sablés, a weekend citron and the pound cakes are flour, butter, egg and sugar without exception, and the shop offers nothing else to eat. A coeliac at this counter is having coffee and only coffee — which is worth knowing in advance rather than discovering at the case. ⚠ AND ONE ITEM NAME REPAYS A SECOND LOOK: 全粒粉サブレ. 全粒粉 is WHOLEMEAL — wheat milled with the bran — and it reads to a lot of people as the grain-conscious or health-food choice on a menu. It is the most wheat-forward biscuit on this list, not the least. The same word appears on the noodles at せきやけ elsewhere in this dataset and means the same thing there. ⚠ ON MILK: the drinks split cleanly between black coffee and dairy, and NO OAT, SOY OR ALMOND MILK APPEARS ANYWHERE on the published menu. That does not prove the counter has none — a barista-staffed specialty shop usually does — but it is not offered in writing, so a vegan should ask rather than assume, and the ミルク at ¥580 is dairy outright.
